find.description: Find issues of the bound GitHub repository by text, semantic state and labels, oldest first, one bounded page at a time. Without a query it reads the issue list; with one it reads GitHub's issue search, whose index trails recent writes. States map to labels through settings.states; find does not report parents.

get.description: Read one issue of the bound GitHub repository, with its parent issue when it has one. A pull request is not a task.

create.description: Open an issue in the bound GitHub repository. The idempotency key is recorded in the issue body as a hidden comment: a repeated key returns the issue it opened, the same key with other content is a conflict, and a create whose outcome is unknown is read back and answered unresolved rather than opened twice. Only an issue the credential's account opened answers for a key; two concurrent calls with one key are not detected.

update.description: Change an issue's title, body or labels. Labels replace the task's labels; state labels change only through transition. expectedRevision is compared with the issue read just before the write: GitHub has no conditional issue write, so a writer between the two is not detected.

transition.description: Move an issue to a semantic state: open states by the labels settings.states names, done and canceled by closing it as completed or not planned. A state without a configured label is unsupported. expectedRevision is compared with the issue read just before the write.

assign.description: Replace an issue's assignees; @me names the credential's account. GitHub drops a login it cannot assign, and the answer lists the actual assignees. An assignee is information, never an exclusive claim: this provider offers no claim.

link.description: Set or remove an issue's parent through GitHub sub-issues. The parent must be an issue of the same repository. The parent is outside the issue's revision: link leaves the revision as it is, so an expectedRevision does not detect a concurrent link.

find.description: Find the pull requests of an exact base and head in the bound GitHub repository; head is a branch of the repository or owner:branch of a fork.

upsert.description: Update the open pull request of an exact base and head, or open it. GitHub keeps one open pull request per base and head, so a repeated or concurrent upsert never opens a second. A requested headCommit must be the commit the head points at. expectedRevision is compared with the pull request read just before the write. settings.assignAuthor adds the account's assignment. settings.inheritLabelPrefixes copies matching labels from related issues named by Closes or Refs in the body; Refs may name another repository on the configured GitHub host. The answer lists the pull request's assignees and labels.

status.description: Read a pull request, the GitHub check runs and commit statuses of its head commit, and its submitted reviews.

review.description: Submit a review of a pull request. The idempotency key is recorded in the review body as a hidden comment: a repeated key returns the review it published, and a review whose outcome is unknown is read back and answered unresolved rather than published twice. Only a review the credential's account submitted answers for a key. GitHub refuses an approval or a change request by the pull request's author.

comments.description: List what people wrote on a pull request, oldest first: the body of each submitted review without the hidden idempotency comment, each comment on a file line with its path, line and commit, both naming their review, then each conversation comment. A review with an empty body is no comment, and a line comment whose line left the diff keeps its path without a line.

merge.description: Merge a pull request whose head is still the expected commit. Refused before anything is sent unless settings.allowMerge is true; binding this provider authorizes nobody to merge.
